questions.question: Asexual reproduction takes place through budding in
questions.explanation: Yeast reproduces asexually by budding — a small outgrowth forms and separates. Amoeba uses binary fission.
questions.chapter_ref: NCERT Class 10 Ch 7 — How do Organisms Reproduce?

questions.question: What is the importance of DNA copying in reproduction?
options: DNA copying is not needed for reproduction
DNA copying ensures offspring receive complete genetic information for body design
DNA copying only happens in sexual reproduction
questions.explanation: DNA must be copied and passed to new cells so offspring inherit instructions for body design and survival.
questions.chapter_ref: NCERT Class 10 Ch 7 — How do Organisms Reproduce?

questions.question: Why is variation beneficial to the species but not necessarily for the individual?
options: Variation helps species survive environmental changes even if some individuals suffer
questions.explanation: Variations create diversity so some individuals may survive if conditions change — benefits species survival.
questions.chapter_ref: NCERT Class 10 Ch 7 — How do Organisms Reproduce?

questions.question: How does binary fission differ from multiple fission?
options: Binary fission produces many cells; multiple fission produces two
Binary fission splits into two; multiple fission produces many daughter cells at once
Multiple fission occurs only in plants
questions.explanation: Binary fission: one cell → two (Amoeba). Multiple fission: one cell → many (Plasmodium).
questions.chapter_ref: NCERT Class 10 Ch 7 — How do Organisms Reproduce?

questions.question: How is the process of pollination different from fertilisation?
options: Pollination is transfer of pollen to stigma; fertilisation is fusion of gametes
questions.explanation: Pollination moves pollen to stigma; fertilisation fuses male and female gametes inside the ovule.
questions.chapter_ref: NCERT Class 10 Ch 7 — How do Organisms Reproduce?

questions.question: What are the changes seen in girls at the time of puberty?
options: Breast development, menstruation begins, wider hips
Only height increases with no other changes
questions.explanation: Puberty in girls includes breast development, onset of menstrual cycle, and wider hips — driven by oestrogen.
questions.chapter_ref: NCERT Class 10 Ch 7 — How do Organisms Reproduce?

questions.question: How will an organism be benefited if it reproduces through spores?
options: Spores are lightweight, easily dispersed, and survive harsh conditions
Spores always produce identical offspring with no variation
questions.explanation: Spores have thick walls, are light and easily spread by air/water, and survive unfavourable conditions.
questions.chapter_ref: NCERT Class 10 Ch 7 — How do Organisms Reproduce?

questions.question: What is the key takeaway about **DNA as genetic material**?
options: Variation is raw material for evolution.
Every cell has DNA; gametes carry half in sexual reproduction
Each daughter cell needs full DNA set.
questions.explanation: Every cell has DNA; gametes carry half in sexual reproduction.

questions.question: What is the key takeaway about **Why DNA copying is needed**?
options: Without DNA transfer, offspring would lack design information

questions.explanation: Without DNA transfer, offspring would lack design information.

questions.question: Which statement best describes **Why organisms reproduce**?
options: Organisms reproduce asexually (one parent) or sexually (two parents) — different DNA mixing outcomes.
DNA copying is remarkably accurate but not absolutely perfect — small errors create variations.
Nutrition, respiration, transport support individual life; reproduction creates new individuals.
Organisms reproduce to create new individuals of their species so life continues generation after generation.
questions.explanation: Reproduction is not for individual survival — it is for species continuity.
